answers.evidence: The module resolves where the factory's state lives. control_dir builds the path from xdg_state_home()/kstrl/repo_id and control_file(root_dir, name) returns a path under it. control_untrusted_reason refuses to trust the directory when it resolves under the repo tree, when a file is a symlink or when the directory is inaccessible. It holds CONTROL_AUTONOMY only as a filename constant and never promotes or demotes anything.

RunSummary, HomeStats, SummaryCache.refresh and gather_stats compute the per-run rows and quick stats that the home screen displays. The docstring says 'Home shell data: run summaries + quick stats (TUI surface D2)', and the module is imported by kstrl.tui.screens.home and kstrl.tui.widgets.run_table. Nothing in it belongs to the ks command tree or calls cli(ctx).

ComponentTable is a Textual DataTable that shows one row per component on the run board. It updates rows in place through update_state and update_cell, and tick_ages refreshes the age column. It is imported by kstrl.tui.screens.home and kstrl.tui.screens.overview. It is a board display, not the console protocol or event renderer behind build_console.

RunContext holds one run's RunTailer, StateStore and TextTailer transcript tailers. The docstring says this state was extracted from KstrlTuiApp so the app can open, close and swap runs. RunContext.observe and transcript_tailer set up the tail that keeps reading the run's files, which matches Dashboard's 'the run it is attached to, and the tail'. The only importer is kstrl.tui.app.

build_console(mode, no_color, ascii_only, force_rich) -> Console matches the card's interface exactly. It picks PlainUI or RichUI through get_ui and connects EventBridgeUI -> EventBus -> CallbackSink -> UIBackedRenderer, which is the path that turns an event into a line on the terminal.

KSTRL_THEME, STATUS_GLYPHS and status_glyph provide the palette and status glyphs that the screens and widgets are drawn with. Nearly all of its 19 importers are kstrl.tui.screens.* or kstrl.tui.widgets.* modules. It is a Textual Theme, not a console back end, so Terminal does not describe it better, and no other card is a clearly better match.

CodexAgent.run(prompt, cwd, timeout) -> Iterator[str] starts the codex CLI through DeadlineStreamer with a timeout. It reads token usage from the 'tokens used' lines at the end of the output (_TOKENS_USED_LINE) into UsageRecord. This is the AgentAdapter interface, and the module does nothing to enforce allowed paths.

ComponentScreen is a Textual Screen for one component's detail view. compose puts together PhaseTimeline, FindingsTable, TranscriptTail and EvidencePanel, and escape (app.pop_screen) goes back. That matches RunViews' 'one component's detail' and 'the phase timeline'.

CompileSourceStep subclasses WorkflowStep with name "compile-source". Its run(ctx) picks a SourceCompiler for each source and merges the results into ctx.compiled_source. That is the first of the four workflow steps. The module never calls an AI provider directly.

This is an auto-generated __init__ that re-exports Pydantic shapes such as HouseholdCreate, ShoppingListOut, ReadWebhook and GroupEventPagination. It has no repository or database access. The fact that repository_household imports it does not change what it is.

It is an operator command: main() parses --workers and --force-all with argparse, asks for y/n confirmation, and runs process_all_recipes. This matches the Scripts card's "rebuild the image sizes". It uses the minifier through RecipeDataService but does not define it.
RecipeSlug is a MealieModel. SlugResponse, UpdateImageResponse and RecipeDuplicate are pydantic BaseModel classes used by the recipe routes. None of them is a SQLAlchemy table.
Nutrition subclasses SqlAlchemyBase with __tablename__ "recipe_nutrition", and its recipe_id column is a ForeignKey to recipes.id. It is one table for one part of a recipe.

main() prompts for a user's email, reads the new password with getpass, hashes it with hash_password and saves it with repos.users.update_password. This is the Scripts card's "change a password" command.

It re-exports Pydantic response and request shapes: PaginationBase, PaginationQuery, ErrorResponse, SuccessResponse and the SSEDataEvent* models. The routes import them. It does not turn filter strings into SQL.
ListItem, ShoppingListIn and ShoppingListOut all subclass MealieModel, and ListItem and ShoppingListOut set from_attributes=True. They are API shapes, not tables or repositories.

No Tantivy or full-text code. resolve_effective_document, get_latest_version_for_root and annotate_effective_content run Django ORM queries over Document.root_document/version_index to resolve document versions, which is document-model logic.

get_workflows_for_trigger(trigger_type, workflow_to_run) fetches enabled Workflow rows for a WorkflowTrigger type with WorkflowAction prefetches for the runner. It has nothing to do with integrity checks or check_sanity.

CustomAccountAdapter (is_open_for_signup, pre_authenticate, save_user with ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_GROUPS) and CustomSocialAccountAdapter are allauth sign-in and social-account hooks. There is no WebSocket or progress code.

Command(BaseCommand).handle is a manage.py command an operator runs by hand to convert Document.transaction_id from CharField to UUIDField via schema_editor.alter_field. It contains no upload or URL safety checks.

generate_object_with_permissions_schema builds drf_spectacular extend_schema for the list/retrieve operations with a full_perms query param, and AngularApiAuthenticationOverrideScheme documents API auth. Both describe the REST API and are imported by documents.views.

_keyword_bounds and _iso_range turn relative date keywords ('previous month', YYYYMM tokens) into Tantivy exclusive range syntax '[lo TO hi}'. It is used by documents.search._translate for query translation.

Defines ParserProtocol, the plugin contract whose supported_mime_types() and score() the registry uses to choose a parser, and which is validated in ParserRegistry.discover. The module states it contains no concrete parser implementations, so FileParsers fits less well.

clamp_applicationconfiguration_integer_fields and AlterField operations change ApplicationConfiguration.barcode_dpi/image_dpi/pages. That is the one-row runtime settings model described by the AppConfig card.

The Poetry class is the in-memory project that Factory.create_poetry returns. It holds the package, the pyproject (PyProjectTOML), the locker, the repository pool and the sources (get_sources). It takes a Config as an input but does not manage the cache, config or data directories, the settings file or environment variable overrides.

LockCommand (name="lock") calls installer.lock(update=regenerate) and then installer.run() to write poetry.lock. The DependencyCommands card names lock explicitly. It does not build, check or publish anything.

Command is the base class for every command. Its poetry property falls back to get_application().poetry, and it also defines set_poetry and reset_poetry. This matches the Cli card's job of giving each command the project it needs. The module does not format log records, colour output or filter by verbosity.

The module re-exports SdistBuilder and WheelBuilder from poetry-core plus EditableBuilder, and defines the BUILD_FORMATS name-to-builder map. This is exactly the Builders card. Nothing in it uploads files, hashes them or looks up credentials.

Source is the dataclass for one [tool.poetry.source] entry (name, url, priority). Poetry.get_sources builds these from pyproject data, and to_toml_table writes one back as a pyproject table. The ProjectLoader card names the project's sources. Nothing here touches the cache, config or data directories, the settings file or environment variables.

PythonVersionNotFoundError ("Could not find the python executable"), NoCompatiblePythonVersionFoundError and InvalidCurrentPythonVersionError are all failures to find a suitable interpreter. The module sits under env.python and is imported by python.manager. env_manager imports it too, but no other card clearly describes this job better.
Under if __name__ == "__main__" it imports main from poetry.console.application and calls sys.exit(main()). This is the python -m poetry entry point that the Cli card names.

SearchCommand (name="search") calls repository.search(tokens) on each repository in poetry.pool.repositories and renders a package/version/source table. The DependencyCommands card lists search explicitly.

The module's main job is making control-code segments. Control.__init__ renders ControlType codes through CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT into Segment(rendered_codes, None, control_codes), and __rich_console__ yields that segment. The Segment card covers this directly ('or a control code'). The module does not print, measure width or choose a colour system, which is the Console card's job.

The module defines Color.parse, which handles ANSI_COLOR_NAMES, hex, color(n) and rgb(). It also defines Color.downgrade, which maps truecolor to EIGHT_BIT, STANDARD or WINDOWS through the palettes. It does no tag or emoji markup parsing.

PromptBase.ask and __call__ loop over console.input. check_choice validates the answer against choices, and process_response converts it with response_type (IntPrompt, FloatPrompt, Confirm). The module contains no logging handler.
legacy_windows_render(buffer, term) turns each Segment into LegacyWindowsTerm Win32 calls such as write_styled, move_cursor_to and erase_line. It produces no HTML or notebook output.

The module defines the module-level print, print_json and inspect. All three use get_console(), which creates one global _console on first use and keeps it. It also re-exports load_ipython_extension. This matches the RichAPI card's interface.
DEFAULT = Theme(DEFAULT_STYLES) is the default mapping of style names to styles. This matches the Style card's statement that 'a theme gives styles names'.

The module defines WINDOWS_PALETTE, STANDARD_PALETTE and EIGHT_BIT_PALETTE. Only rich.color imports them, and Color.downgrade uses them through STANDARD_PALETTE.match and WINDOWS_PALETTE.match. These are 'the standard palettes' named in the Color card.

Theme maps names to Style objects by calling Style.parse on string values. Theme.from_file and Theme.read load those names from config files, and ThemeStack.get looks a style up by name. This is the naming role in the Style card.
